newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bureaucrats who refuse to cede power and resist decentralisation are the main obstacle to reform, the prime minister says. Bureaucratic reform would fail unless they changed their ways, says General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who identified decentralisation of power as the core element of the drive. (BANGKOK POST)

- New Aspiration Party MP Chattawat Mutamara has given himself up to fight charges of having cheated the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) out of nearly one billion baht - ending a week-long hide-and-seek game with investigators. Chattawat is released on a 10 million baht bail bond after being questioned for more than three hours. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Villagers in Pluak Daeng in Rayong province have won their battle to keep a hazardous waste landfill site out of their district. Pluak Daeng, the scene of intense local opposition to the General Conservation Co project, will instead be designated an environmental conservation area. (BANGKOK POST)

- Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond has signalled that commercial banks will further cut interest rates in the coming weeks after already reducing rates by 0.25 of a percentage point. However, the governor's signal remains mixed because the central bank has insisted on maintaining its discount rate, the rate at which it lends to commercial banks, at 10.5 per cent. (THE NATION)

- The Cabinet will consider today a proposal to allow foreigners or foreign businesses to own up to 49 percent of the units in condominium projects, an increase from the current 40 percent. The amendment to the Condominium Act of 1979 has been proposed by Interior Minister Sanoh Thienthong. (BANGKOK POST)
